details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:26-27,160 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: Line 26 tells the agent to resolve overlaps by replacing the shared piece in one plan with a cross-reference. Line 27 and Rules line 160 say any scope change is NEEDS DECISION and never applied. The text also never says which plan keeps the shared piece.
  WHY: The instructions conflict, so runs will diverge. Some will deduplicate and others will mark NEEDS DECISION. Severity is MAJOR from all reviewers.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:153-154 (vs 59, 65) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `Edit` grant covers only step-4a `docs/plans/*` refreshes "and nothing else". Step 8 requires deleting an entry from `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`, and step 9 requires creating a `changelog.d/` fragment. Neither write fits the grant. Minimax and GLM also note that the Bash grant does not cover them either.
  WHY: An agent that follows the declared scope literally cannot complete steps 8-9. Otherwise it breaks the scope. Minimax and GLM also raised this under trust-boundary risks as the same defect, and Sonnet raised it as a NIT, so the highest severity (MAJOR) is used.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:23-28,39,52 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The refresh-edit bullet comes before the tracking-issue listing fetch that the in-flight guard depends on. No rule covers a failed or missing listing. Step 6 line 39 reuses the listing with no fallback, and the degraded mode at line 52 does not cover a missing step-4a listing.
  WHY: The agent may edit plans that an open orchestrator project already uses. Step 6 may also screen candidates against an absent listing.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:154 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The Bash bullet allows the step-4a `git fetch` but then bans "mutating git operations outside steps 7–9". `git fetch` updates remote-tracking refs.
  WHY: An agent that treats the ban as the hard bound skips the fetch, and the drift check runs against a stale `origin/<default>`.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:159-160 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The hand-off sentence ("To act on the recommendation, the user runs `/implement-plan-claude` … or `/implement-plan-ai` …") moved out of the "Report-first" rule and into the new "A refresh adapts the plan, never its intent" rule. The same text is in the workflow-templates copy.
  WHY: The Report-first rule no longer says what to do with the recommendation, and the hand-off guidance now reads as part of the refresh rule.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: The PR description says the audit makes sure "the next plan handed off matches the repo as it is now". Refreshes land in the step 9 maintenance PR.
  expected_change_site: .claude/commands/audit-plans.md (and the workflow-templates copy): the Output Format "Maintenance:" line (116), the "➡ Next highest-value to implement" block (118-121), the bundle "Hand off:" line (133), and step 9 (63-68).
  confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: Refreshed plans sit on an unmerged maintenance branch and PR, so the default branch still holds the stale text. No hunk tells the user the recommended plan was refreshed on an unmerged branch, or gates the hand-off on the maintenance PR merging. `.claude/commands/implement-plan-ai.md` step 3 reads the plan from the default branch, so an early hand-off uses the stale copy. `tests/test_audit_plans_command.py` asserts no such precondition.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:26,27,160 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Line 26 replaces the shared piece in one plan with a cross-reference. Line 27 and Rules line 160 say scope changes are NEEDS DECISION. The text does not say which plan keeps the shared piece.
  WHY: An agent cannot obey both instructions, so runs will pick different owners or never deduplicate.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:153 (vs 59, 65) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `Edit` grant is limited to step-4a plan refreshes "and nothing else". Step 8 (registry deletion) and step 9 (changelog fragment) are file writes outside it.
  WHY: An agent that follows Tool Access literally cannot make those writes.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:26-28,39 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The in-flight guard depends on the tracking-issue listing, which is fetched after the edit bullet. No rule covers a failed or unreadable listing, and step 6 line 39 has no fallback.
  WHY: The agent may edit plans that an orchestrator project is already running from, and step 6 may screen against an absent listing. The command should fail closed.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:154 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The bullet allows the step-4a `git fetch`, then forbids mutating git operations outside steps 7–9.
  WHY: An agent that skips the fetch compares plans against a stale `origin/<default>` with no error.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md (and workflow-templates copy):159-160 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The hand-off sentence was removed from the "Report-first" bullet and appended to the new refresh bullet.
  WHY: The hand-off guidance now reads as part of the refresh-boundary rule.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:153-154 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The declared write scope ("nothing else", plus `git fetch` against the ban) does not match the effective one.
  WHY: This is the same defect as the findings above and is not a separate one.
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: the next plan handed off matches the repo as it is now; refreshes land in the step 9 maintenance PR.
  Expected change site: .claude/commands/audit-plans.md and the workflow-templates copy: the Output Format "Maintenance:" block, the "➡ Next highest-value to implement" and bundle `Hand off:` lines, and step 9.
  Evidence of absence: Refreshed plans sit on an unmerged maintenance branch, and no hunk warns the user or gates the hand-off on the merge. `tests/test_audit_plans_command.py` asserts no such precondition.
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
- HARDENING: .claude/commands/audit-plans.md, step 4a "Plans in flight" bullet and the Tool Access `Edit` bullet. Move the tracking-issue fetch ahead of the refresh bullet. Add "if the listing cannot be read, report plans as UNVERIFIED and make no refresh edits". Reword `Edit` to cover the step-4a refresh, the step-8 registry deletion and the step-9 changelog fragment. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

  WHY: The Report-first rule no longer says what to do with the recommendation, and future hand-off changes will look in the wrong rule.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:26,27,160 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4

  WHY: Runs diverge, and a reviewer cannot tell whether a cross-reference edit was authorized.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:23-28 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The refresh bullet comes before the in-flight check and the listing fetch it depends on.
  WHY: An agent reading in order may refresh plans an open `ai:orchestrator-tracking` issue names. `test_tracking_issue_listing_is_fetched_once` does not assert the order within step 4a.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:153 (vs 59, 65) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `Edit` scope covers only `docs/plans/*`. Step 8 registry deletion and step 9 fragment creation fall outside it. `git rm` cannot delete one registry entry, and Bash has no path for creating a fragment.
  WHY: An agent that follows the scope literally cannot do steps 8-9. Otherwise it breaks the scope.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:154 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The bullet allows the step-4a `git fetch`, then bans mutating git operations outside steps 7–9.
  WHY: An agent that skips the fetch weakens the drift check silently.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:28,39,52 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The step-4a listing fetch has no fallback when it cannot be read or never runs. Step 6 reuses it with no fallback, and the degraded mode covers only step-6 failures.
  WHY: Refresh edits may hit in-flight plans, and step 6 may either re-fetch or skip the conflict gate.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:153 (vs 59, 65) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: This is the declared-vs-effective capability gap seen from the trust-boundary angle. The `Edit` scope forecloses writes the procedure requires.
  WHY: A scoped agent either drops a required write or breaks the declared scope.
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: PR goal — "the next plan handed off matches the repo as it is now."
  Expected change site: .claude/commands/audit-plans.md Output Format "Maintenance:" block (116), "➡ Next highest-value to implement:" block (118-121), bundle "Hand off:" line (133), and the no-recommendation block (139-141). Mirror in `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md`.
  Evidence of absence: The step 9 maintenance PR is unmerged when the Output Format is emitted. No hunk warns the user. `.claude/commands/implement-plan-ai.md` reads the plan from the default branch (step 3), so an early hand-off reads the stale text. `tests/test_audit_plans_command.py` has no assertion for this.
  severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
- HARDENING: NONE (the diff is docs-only).
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
